summary: Backend video_id/video_kind extraction is FULLY VERIFIED — all 11 pytest tests pass (video list, /wp/posts/16163 returns exactly video_id='pNxobWWrWys' + video_kind='youtube', non-video posts have null fields, and _extract_video() handles all 5 documented URL shapes: youtube.com/embed/, youtu.be/, youtube.com/watch?v=, youtube-nocookie.com/embed/, player.vimeo.com/video/). However, the frontend web preview is now COMPLETELY BROKEN by this same fix — Metro fails to bundle the web build because src/components/VideoPlayer.tsx does `require('react-native-youtube-iframe')` inside a runtime `Platform.OS !== 'web'` branch, but Metro statically walks all require() calls at bundle time. On web, react-native-youtube-iframe resolves to its WebView.web.js which imports 'react-native-web-webview' (NOT installed). Result: /node_modules/expo-router/entry.bundle returns HTTP 500, every route renders as a blank white page, and the entire app is unusable on web (including the Videos-tab → tap-card flow the review explicitly asked to verify). Bundle error confirmed in /var/log/supervisor/expo.out.log: `Unable to resolve "react-native-web-webview" from "node_modules/react-native-youtube-iframe/lib/commonjs/WebView.web.js"`.

action_items: FIX WEB BUNDLE (blocker): Split VideoPlayer into platform-specific files. Option A (recommended): create /app/frontend/src/components/VideoPlayer.web.tsx (contains only the iframe branch, no require of react-native-youtube-iframe) and rename the current file to VideoPlayer.native.tsx (contains only the native branch). Option B: install `react-native-web-webview` as a dependency so youtube-iframe's WebView.web.js resolves — but this pulls extra weight into the web bundle and doesn't fix the fact that react-native-youtube-iframe's web variant is a lower-fidelity player than the plain iframe you already have.

The Platform.OS conditional in VideoPlayer.tsx is a common but risky pattern — Metro does not honor it as a static tree-shake. The idiomatic fix is a .web/.native file split. Using `require()` inside an `if` block is misleading; readers assume it's lazy but Metro resolves it at bundle time.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of the frontend regression: React Native's Metro bundler resolves require() calls at bundle time, not runtime. Wrapping `require('react-native-youtube-iframe')` in `if (Platform.OS !== 'web')` does NOT prevent Metro from resolving the module for the web bundle. Metro walks every require() reachable in the module graph and tries to resolve it for the target platform. On web, react-native-youtube-iframe resolves to its `WebView.web.js` file which does `require('react-native-web-webview')` — a package that isn't in package.json and isn't in node_modules. Metro fails the whole bundle with a 500. Reproduction: `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'https://wisdom-edge.preview.emergentagent.com/node_modules/expo-router/entry.bundle?platform=web&dev=true&hot=false&lazy=true&transform.engine=hermes&transform.routerRoot=app'` → 500. Mitigation (recommended): rename VideoPlayer.tsx → VideoPlayer.native.tsx (keeps only the native YouTube iframe code) and create a new VideoPlayer.tsx (or VideoPlayer.web.tsx) that contains ONLY the <iframe> branch and does not require the youtube-iframe package at all. Metro's platform-file resolution will select VideoPlayer.web.tsx (or fall through to VideoPlayer.tsx) on web builds and VideoPlayer.native.tsx on iOS/Android/Expo Go. This is a two-file, zero-behavior-change split. Not done here because it changes source-tree layout, which is main-agent territory.
